inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Chuckling through the words, playful sing-song lilt, mock-theatrical delivery aimed at the gasp itself.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Makes the other speaker's reaction the joke, when the gasp was sincere shock about a real chance.

parsed.acceptable_range_note: Anything from bright shared excitement to brisk practical urgency to calm steady reassurance works, at high or quite contained energy.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Sharp, fast onset, rising pitch, clipped breathy delivery like reacting to an emergency or bad news breaking.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: The mystery just resolved harmlessly; the sigh releases tension rather than raising it.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Peppy, upswinging, smiling-through-every-word delivery with announcer-like energy, as if sharing delightful news.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Overshoots the deflated, mildly exasperated valence of the sigh and reads as tone-deaf enthusiasm.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Slow, hushed, weighted delivery with sombre downward contours, the register used for genuine loss or bad diagnoses.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Treats a missing cake as a serious misfortune, inflating a small domestic annoyance into grief.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Flat, clipped, faintly exasperated-at-the-listener delivery, sighing back or trailing off as though the topic is tiresome.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Turns shared exasperation into irritation aimed at the speaker, withdrawing from a moment they invited.

parsed.acceptable_range_note: Wry amusement, gentle warmth, dry matter-of-factness, quiet commiseration, or a soft laugh all fit, at low-to-moderate energy.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Sharp, loud, fast onset; tight throat, urgent clipped delivery as though reporting danger or a genuine crisis.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: The mystery has just resolved harmlessly; treating the reveal as threatening overshoots a moment that has released its tension.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Even pitch, no lift or fall, unhurried and affectless, as if reading an unrelated line off a page.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Registers nothing of the sudden reveal the other speaker just reacted to, leaving the gasp hanging unacknowledged.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Slowed, softened, singsong lilt with drawn-out vowels, the cadence used to calm someone who is overreacting.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Casts the other speaker as needing management rather than as a partner who just solved the puzzle with you.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Clipped, downward-tailing delivery, possibly a short exhale through the nose; brisk and closed, shutting the exchange down.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Brushes off a discovery both speakers were actively working toward, treating the other's surprise as not worth meeting.

parsed.acceptable_range_note: Anything from quiet dawning realisation to amused disbelief to relieved exhalation works, at low or lively energy, with or without a laugh.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Fast, tight, rising delivery with sharp breath intake and clipped emphasis, as though announcing an emergency.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: The sigh signals weary acceptance of a manageable hassle, not crisis; urgency escalates past what the moment holds.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Lifted, sing-song energy with an upbeat lilt and smile audible through the voice.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Brightness contradicts the deflated valence of the sigh and reads as ignoring the other speaker's fatigue.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Laughter in the voice, playful bounce, or a chuckle riding under the words.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Treats a resigned exhalation about a hurt child as a shared joke, misreading its valence entirely.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Exaggeratedly soft, drawn-out, singsong comforting pitched as if speaking to a small child.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Casts the fellow adult as needing management; the sigh invites shared practicality, not being talked down to.

parsed.acceptable_range_note: Anything from a quiet matching exhale to calm steady practicality, gentle warmth, or brisk get-on-with-it resolve is fine.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Breathy chuckle or smile in the voice, playful lift on the words, delivery that treats the gasp as funny.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Reads the gasp as comic surprise rather than the alarmed recognition of something wrong in a hurt child's mouth.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Sharp intake, rising pitch and volume, rushed clipped phrasing, audible tremor as if announcing an emergency.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Amplifies the shock past what the moment holds; the parent has already steadied toward a next step, not spiralled.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Level monotone, no change in pace or warmth from earlier turns, words delivered like a scheduling note.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Registers nothing at all in response to a gasp, as though the discovery had not landed.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Cooing sing-song, drawn-out vowels, shushing hush, over-soft cadence of the kind used to calm a small child.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Treats the co-parent as needing to be managed rather than as someone seeing the same thing.

parsed.acceptable_range_note: Anything from a quiet, steady, concerned register to a visibly startled but collected one is fine, whether brisk and practical or slow and hushed.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Even, clipped delivery with no lift or warmth, like reading a number back off a form.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Treats a life-changing, disbelieving moment as routine data entry, leaving the other person's stunned reaction unmet.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Short, throwaway delivery with a shrug in the voice, trailing off as if the topic is closing.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Waves away a moment the speaker is visibly struggling to absorb, and their sigh invites acknowledgment, not dismissal.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Tight, fast, high-strung voice with sharp breath, as though reporting an emergency or bad news.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Reads the sigh as distress or catastrophe rather than the overwhelm of something extraordinary and good.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Slow, singsong, caregiver-style softening, as if calming a distressed child.

parsed.acceptable_range_note: Anything from hushed disbelief to bright excitement to a quiet steady confirmation works, as long as the delivery registers that something remarkable just happened.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Even, level delivery with no lift or energy change from earlier turns; reads like confirming a grocery item.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Treats a life-changing shock as routine information, leaving the other speaker's gasp hanging unmet.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Tight, sharp, breath-caught voice with rising panic; the pitch of bad news breaking.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Flat drawl, light scoff or eye-roll audible in the voice, trailing off as if unimpressed.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Belittles a genuinely astonishing moment the responder just helped confirm and was equally invested in.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Slow, hushed, downward-settling delivery, as if gentling someone who is overreacting.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Frames the gasp as distress needing management rather than warranted amazement.

parsed.acceptable_range_note: Anything from an explosive shared shout to a stunned, quiet, breath-held disbelief works, as long as astonishment is audible and positive.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Upswinging, grinning delivery with excited emphasis and lifted final pitch, the voice you'd use for good news.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Reads a deflated moment as a win; the sigh signals disappointment, not something to be pleased about.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Sharp, fast, raised volume with a startled catch, as if reporting an emergency.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Escalates a minor training setback into a crisis far beyond the low-key resignation the sigh conveys.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Clipped, uninflected, low-energy delivery that trails off, no warmth or acknowledgement in the voice.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Exaggerated cooing melody, drawn-out vowels, pitch lifted as if comforting a small child.

parsed.acceptable_range_note: Wry amusement, warm sympathy, matter-of-fact commiseration, a light laugh, or a quiet understated remark all work; energy may be low or moderately animated.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Sharp intake, raised volume, clipped fast delivery as if reporting danger or an accident in progress.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Upswinging, peppy singsong delivery with smiling brightness, like announcing good news at the top of the turn.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Monotone, low-energy, faintly bored throwaway delivery with no warmth or engagement in the voice.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Slow, syrupy, over-soft consoling voice with exaggerated sympathetic dips, as if comforting a distressed child.

parsed.acceptable_range_note: Wry amusement, mild commiseration, dry matter-of-factness, a sympathetic sigh, or brief warm understatement are all fine; energy may be low or lively.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Tight, rushed, higher-strung voice with anxious over-emphasis, as though something serious went wrong.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Curt, dropped-off delivery with no warmth, cutting in fast as if the exchange is a nuisance.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Slowed, cooing, sing-song comfort voice with exaggerated gentleness, as if consoling a child.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Tightened, fast, higher-pressure voice with worried breathiness, as though something has gone seriously wrong.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Flat, curt, edged delivery, slight sigh of impatience, cutting off warmth as if the groan were an imposition.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Takes an adversarial stance toward a mild complaint that was immediately followed by cooperation.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Slow, sing-song, over-gentle consoling voice, the kind used to settle a upset child.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Treats a minor gripe as real hurt needing comfort, condescending to an adult who already agreed.

parsed.acceptable_range_note: Wry commiseration, a light apologetic shrug, matter-of-fact confirmation, a small shared sigh, or dry amusement all work; brief and understated is fine.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Lifted, smiling delivery with rising energy and a peppy lilt, as if hearing welcome news.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Tightened, fast, breathy delivery with sharp emphasis, as if reacting to bad news of real consequence.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Unvarying pitch, clipped and quick, no warmth or acknowledgement in the voice before moving on.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Slowed, cooing, sing-song comfort voice with softened consonants, the register used for consoling a child.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Takes a caretaking stance over a peer sharing an equally trivial letdown.

parsed.acceptable_range_note: Anything from a wry amused huff, to warm mild commiseration, to a quiet deflated murmur or a brief matter-of-fact shrug, works fine.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Lifted pitch, smiling delivery, energetic bounce on the words, as if announcing good news.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Sharp intake, tightened voice, rushed and loud, pitch climbing as though something serious happened.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Clipped, cool delivery, faint sigh of impatience or a told-you-so lilt directed at the other speaker.

parsed.acceptable_range_note: Anything from a commiserating sigh or wry amused huff to a brief deflated murmur or dry resigned understatement works fine here.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Lifted, sing-song delivery with an upward bounce at the end, smiling energy, quickened pace, as if reporting welcome news.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Treats a deflated, anticlimactic moment as something to be pleased about, running audibly counter to the sigh's low valence.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Tightened, breathy voice, sudden loudness or clipped rapid phrasing, hushed gravity as if delivering an emergency.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Slow, hushed, honeyed caregiving voice with cooing warmth and drawn-out vowels, as though comforting deep grief.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Inflates a passing sigh into serious upset and speaks down to the other person as fragile.

parsed.acceptable_range_note: Flat and matter-of-fact, quietly wry, mildly commiserating, or briefly low-energy agreement are all fine, with or without an answering sigh.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Lifted, smiling delivery with upward endings and bouncy pace, as if reacting to welcome news.
inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Reads the groan's negative valence as positive, so the reply sounds pleased at the other speaker's exasperation.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Sharp intake, tightened and faster speech, raised volume, the register used for emergencies or bad medical news.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Clipped, throwaway delivery with a small scoff or amused huff aimed at the other speaker.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Slow, hushed, weighted phrasing with long pauses, the cadence reserved for condolence.

inappropriate_tones.why_wrong: Overshoots a quiet one-to-one exchange deliberately staged before other people arrive, performing at rather than responding to the speaker.

parsed.acceptable_range_note: Anything from a warm laughing pleasure through sly teasing to quiet, understated satisfaction or gentle brushing-off works, at conversational volume and closeness.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Even pitch, no lift or breath, steady low energy, as if reading a line unrelated to what just happened.

inappropriate_tones.sounds_like: Shrieking or loud exaggerated wonder, big swooping pitch swings, sustained volume far exceeding the moment's scale.
